page.layout: One page of text, with running head and page number at the top. No margin notes. Reading order: the first paragraph (continued from the previous page), the heading "EPIST. LXXXVI.", the argument line, the address to Cardinal Barberino, and the opening of the letter.

main_text.p: sa celebretur? Respondeo, semel tantum missam celebrari in die super idem altare, nisi vel adsi urgeatque necessitas aliqua, vel id Episcopi obtineatur auctoritate. Vale Doctissime atque Doctissime Vir meque tui colentissimum amare perge. Romæ 13. Julii 1654.

Quæstiunculis hisce tuis utcunque po-tui respondi. nunc restat, ut etiam atque etiam te rogem, ne meam hanc responsionem edas, & in eruditorum evulges theatrum; at si hoc tibi aliquo modo libuerit, eam ut castiges, enixe efflagito, ac tua summa eruditione, sapientiaque limatam facias addendo, diminuendo mutando, expoliendoque, ut proprius auctor, & amici perhumaniter ignoscas ruditati.
main_text.head: EPIST. LXXXVI.
J. Morinus Card. Barberino commendat negotia aliqua suæ Congregationis.
main_text.p: RPater Valencon nomine, qui has litteras Emin. Vestræ reddit, Con-grega-

page.notes: The first line of the page is a fragment ("sa celebretur?") continuing from the previous page. The large R at the start of the last paragraph is a drop initial, joined to "Pater". Old-style figures appear in the date ("13" and "1654"). Long s is printed throughout and is transcribed as s. The word "ruditati" is clear on the scan. A small stray mark appears at the top left above the running head; it is not text. The last line ends with a word broken across pages ("Con-grega-"). No catchword or signature is printed.
